raw: {"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"The dot product measures how much one vector points along another. For nonzero b, drop a perpendicular from the tip of a to the line through b. The signed distance from the common starting point to where it lands is the scalar projection of a onto b. Multiply that distance by the length of b: a · b = ‖a‖ ‖b‖ cos θ, where θ is the angle between the vectors."},{"type":"ui","source":"root = Stack([diagram])\ndiagram = Graphic(\"Signed projection of a onto b\",[{kind:\"text\",x:12,y:20,text:\"Positive\"},{kind:\"text\",x:161,y:20,text:\"Orthogonal\"},{kind:\"text\",x:311,y:20,text:\"Negative\"},{kind:\"path\",d:\"M 25 96 H 130 M 122 91 L 130 96 L 122 101 M 25 96 L 87 43 M 77 45 L 87 43 L 84 53 M 87 50 V 58 M 87 63 V 71 M 87 76 V 84 M 87 89 V 96\"},{kind:\"text\",x:93,y:44,text:\"a\"},{kind:\"text\",x:118,y:84,text:\"b\"},{kind:\"text\",x:64,y:119,text:\"a · b > 0\"},{kind:\"path\",d:\"M 180 96 H 279 M 271 91 L 279 96 L 271 101 M 180 96 V 42 M 175 50 L 180 42 L 185 50 M 180 85 H 191 V 96\"},{kind:\"text\",x:190,y:47,text:\"a\"},{kind:\"text\",x:267,y:84,text:\"b\"},{kind:\"text\",x:204,y:119,text:\"a · b = 0\"},{kind:\"path\",d:\"M 314 96 H 431 M 423 91 L 431 96 L 423 101 M 369 96 L 327 43 M 329 53 L 327 43 L 337 47 M 327 50 V 58 M 327 63 V 71 M 327 76 V 84 M 327 89 V 96\"},{kind:\"text\",x:315,y:43,text:\"a\"},{kind:\"text\",x:419,y:84,text:\"b\"},{kind:\"text\",x:351,y:119,text:\"a · b < 0\"}])","state":[]},{"type":"text","text":"If the projection lands in the direction b points, the dot product is positive. If the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), it lands at the starting point, so the dot product is zero. If it lands on the opposite side, the projection and dot product are negative. A dot product with the zero vector is also zero, even though the angle is undefined."}]}

request: What does BYOK mean in a model-powered application?
raw: {"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"BYOK stands for “Bring Your Own Key.” In a model-powered application, it usually means you supply an API key from your own model provider account instead of using the app’s credentials. Build an interactive weighted comparison of Native Hybrid [9,8,7], Tauri [7,8,8], and Electron [6,4,10]. The three criteria are native experience, lightweight runtime, delivery efficiency. Start with integer weights 40,25,35. Normalize by their sum, rank descending, and show no ranking if all weights are zero. Scores are synthetic.
raw:
{
  "version": "2b1",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Compare Native Hybrid, Tauri, and Electron using synthetic scores. Each weight is an integer from 0 to 100 points and is divided by the total weight before scoring. The ranking is highest score first and stays empty when all three weights are zero."
    },
    {
      "type": "ui",
      "source": "root = Stack([nativeWeight, runtimeWeight, deliveryWeight, totalWeight, rankingLabel, ranking])
$native = 40
$runtime = 25
$delivery = 35
nativeWeight = Control("Native experience (weight points)", 0, 100, [], $native)
runtimeWeight = Control("Lightweight runtime (weight points)", 0, 100, [], $runtime)
deliveryWeight = Control("Delivery efficiency (weight points)", 0, 100, [], $delivery)
total = @Sum([$native, $runtime, $delivery])
totalWeight = Metric("Total weight (points)", total)
divisor = total == 0 ? 1 : total
nativeHybrid = (9 * $native + 8 * $runtime + 7 * $delivery) / divisor
tauri = (7 * $native + 8 * $runtime + 8 * $delivery) / divisor
electron = (6 * $native + 4 * $runtime + 10 * $delivery) / divisor
rows = [{label:"Native Hybrid",score:nativeHybrid},{label:"Tauri",score:tauri},{label:"Electron",score:electron}]
rankedRows = total == 0 ? [] : @Sort(rows,"score","desc")
rankingLabel = Text("Ranking by weighted score (out of 10)")
ranking = Table(rankedRows)",
      "state": []
    }
  ]
}
